events.title: The canonization of John XXIII and John Paul II
events.shortBlurb: On Divine Mercy Sunday, two twentieth-century popes were declared saints together…
body: On 27 April 2014, Divine Mercy Sunday, Pope Francis canonized John XXIII and John Paul II in a single ceremony in St. Peter's Square, before several hundred thousand pilgrims; the retired Benedict XVI concelebrated, the first canonization at which a reigning and a former pope stood together at the altar.

John XXIII, born Angelo Roncalli at Sotto il Monte near Bergamo in 1881, reigned from 1958 to 1963; he summoned the Second Vatican Council, opening it on 11 October 1962, and published the encyclical Pacem in Terris weeks before his death. For him Francis waived the customary second miracle.

John Paul II, born Karol Wojtyła at Wadowice in Poland in 1920, reigned from 1978 until his death on 2 April 2005, one of the longest pontificates in history; he was canonized nine years later, after the healing of a Costa Rican woman, Floribeth Mora, was ascribed to his intercession. He himself had established the feast on which they were canonized.

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of Sts. John XXIII and John Paul II (vatican.va)
